Print the assembled prompt

preview.Rd

Prints the exact string the model will receive, before Ollama applies the model's chat template. Makes no model calls. Prompt failures do not appear in the output of measure().

Usage

preview(
  instrument,
  text = "[document text goes here]",
  item = NULL,
  image = NULL,
  truncate = 300L
)

Arguments

instrument

An instrument().

text

An example document. A short placeholder by default.

item

A string naming the item to show. Defaults to the first.

image

A character vector of paths, one or several, to the media the run would send, or NULL (the default) to send none. A video window is a vector of frame paths. Their presence removes the document block from the prompt, since an image corpus has no text to quote, and adds a bracketed line above it. That line is shown and never sent. Anything in square brackets here describes what travels beside the prompt rather than quoting what is inside it.

truncate

An integer giving the number of characters of document text to show. NULL shows all. The returned string always carries the whole document. Default is 300.

Value

Invisibly, the assembled prompt string for the item shown, exactly as measure() sends it, before Ollama applies the model's chat template. It carries the whole document and leaves out the bracketed media line. A single character scalar.

The printed output and the return value differ, and the difference matters. Printing trims a long document at truncate and shows, beneath the prompt, the table of what each label will be matched against. That table is where most extraction failures are visible, and it is not in the returned string.

So capture the value to diff two prompts or to paste one into a paper, and read the printed output to check the instrument. No call is made either way.

The matching table

The table underneath has two columns. On the left the label, on the right every token that will be counted as that label. They read the same when a label is its own only variant, which is the usual arrangement. They diverge once accented forms are supplied, and again after probing registers whatever token a split label actually emits.

Under prefix matching the right column is not the whole story, since a token also counts when it merely opens one of those forms. BU counts as BUDGET without appearing there. The instrument header says which rule is in force.

See also

instrument() for the prompt's parts and measure() for sending it.

Examples

b <- instrument(
  template_items("topic", c(econ = "the economy", immig = "immigration"),
                 medium = "text"),
  labels = c("YES", "NO")
)
preview(b)
#> Prompt preview
#> 
#> Item          econ, 1 of 2
#> Scoring       generated position 1
#> 
#> ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#> Text: "[document text goes here]"
#> 
#> Does this text discuss the economy?
#> 
#> Answer with exactly one word: YES or NO.
#> 
#> Answer:
#> ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#> 
#> Label         Counts as
#> YES           YES
#> NO            NO
